newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: AGROBANKA HQ SAYS SLOVAK TRANSFER POSSIBLY DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: AGROBANKA HQ SAYS SLOVAK TRANSFER POSSIBLY DELAYED.

text.p: Czech Agrobanka a.s. on Wednesday said the temporary forced administration which the Czech central bank imposed on it might delay the transfer of its Slovak branches into a fully independent Slovak bank.
"After the end of the forced adminstration, (Agrobanka) might have a new owner, and it would decide as it wants to" Agrobanka spokesman Milan Srb told Reuters from the headquarters in Prague.
Earlier, Vranislav Petroch, Agrobanka's Slovak director, said Agrobanka hoped to have the independent Slovak bank, which would go by a new name, operating by the first of January.
The plan would be for Agrobanka Czech Republic to hold 34 percent of the new bank's basic equity of one billion crowns with five large Slovak companies holding the remainder.

On Tuesday, the Czech parent was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank (CNB) because of poor liquidity stemming from the failure of another Czech bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..

Officials from the Czech central bank said on Wednesday they were reviewing the ownership structure of Agrobanka and specifically the Czech investment group Motoinvest which had strong ties to shareholders of Kreditni and Agrobanka.
Srb said the plan to make the Slovak branches independent had been in the works for several months.
Petroch said at a banking conference in central Slovakia that an application was made in August to the National Bank of Slovakia for a full banking licence.
The companies, which Petroch declined to specifically name, would be "lucrative Slovak companies from the chemical industry", he said.
Petroch added that the Slovak operations of Agrobanka were "fully liquid and fully capable of fulfilling any requests by clients".
